question: I need a way to prevent a purchase or payment from triggering a penalty when my everyday spending account comes up short by using funds from another account I already have at the same bank. What are the setup requirements and are there any charges for moving the money?
answer: If you have a Chase savings account, you can link it as a backup to your checking account. Then, if you have enough money in your savings account, we’ll transfer the exact amount needed to cover an overdraft transaction. There’s no cost to enroll and there is no fee to transfer money between accounts.

reference_chunks.content:
## Optional overdraft services
You can enroll in these services to help avoid potential Overdraft Fees.
### Overdraft Protection
If you have a Chase savings account, you can link it as a backup to your checking account. Then, if you have enough money in your savings account, we’ll transfer the exact amount needed to cover an overdraft transaction. There’s no cost to enroll and there is no fee to transfer money between accounts.

question: Should I cash out my points now or save them for a trip if I might close my card soon?
answer: The best time to redeem your cash back rewards is when it makes the most financial sense for you. Most credit card rewards don’t expire so long as your card remains open and in good standing. In general, points are worth more when redeemed for travel through the Chase Travel portal or transferred to Chase’s partners. If you’re interested in cash back, each point is worth 1 cent when redeemed.

# How to know when to redeem credit card rewards
## Quick insights
- The best time to redeem your cash back rewards is when it makes the most financial sense for you.
- You may have several ways to redeem your credit card rewards, with travel and cash back being two common options.
- Most credit card rewards don’t expire so long as your card remains open and in good standing.
People love options, so if you’re looking to redeem credit card rewards, you’re probably in luck. Most cards today offer several ways you can redeem rewards including everything from cash back to discounted travel and entertainment. In this article, we’ll discuss common rewards programs and what you may want to consider if you’re trying to determine when to redeem your rewards.

reference_chunks.content:
## How much are Chase Ultimate Rewards points worth?
The value of your Chase Ultimate rewards points will differ depending on the credit card that you have and the category that you’re redeeming in. In general, points are worth more when redeemed for travel through the Chase Travel portal or transferred to Chase’s partners. If you’re interested in cash back, each point is worth 1 cent when redeemed.

question: Chase spending rewards category limits rules
answer: Cash back credit cards accrue rewards when you make purchases within specific categories (such as grocery stores or gas stations) on the card. There are important differences in what kinds of spending get rewarded and what format the rewards take, such as rotating categories and the value of points. You may also have to keep in mind that some cash back credit cards specify a maximum number of cash back you can earn within a specific time period.

metadata.page_title: What does cash back on credit cards mean? | Chase
metadata.heading_path: What are credit card cash back rewards? > How do cash back credit cards work?

reference_chunks.content:
## How do cash back credit cards work?
Cash back credit cards accrue rewards when you make purchases within specific categories (such as grocery stores or gas stations) on the card. There are important differences in what kinds of spending get rewarded and what format the rewards take, such as rotating categories and the value of points. You may also have to keep in mind that some cash back credit cards specify a maximum number of cash back you can earn within a specific time period.

question: What does a parent need to have to open the Chase account that lets teens get direct deposits?
answer: Chase High School Checking℠ lets them "get direct deposits." "The parent must have an existing qualifying Chase checking account which must be linked to the High School Checking account. Qualifying accounts exclude Chase High School Checking, Chase College Checking, Chase Secure Checking and Chase First Checking."

## Banking that grows with your family
Chase helps you meet your family members where they are in their financial journey:
- Teach your child money basics with Chase First Banking℠
- Let them send money to friends and get direct deposits with Chase High School Checking℠
- Encourage their financial independence with Chase Secure Banking℠ ($0 Monthly Service Fee for 17-24 year olds)
Plus, add on a Chase Savings℠ account to start building healthy saving habits.

metadata.page_title: Chase High School Checking Account | Student Banking | Chase

reference_chunks.content:
## FAQs
Chase High School Checking is for student ages 13-17 at account opening with their parent/guardian as a co-owner. The parent must have an existing qualifying Chase checking account which must be linked to the High School Checking account. Qualifying accounts exclude Chase High School Checking, Chase College Checking, Chase Secure Checking and Chase First Checking.
High School Checking has no monthly service fee. Standard Overdraft Practice and Chase Debit Card Coverage℠ aren't available.
